recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-26685 unless BR&R opens a new issue based on implementer experience that changes the lifecycle or marketing-status model.
issue_request: FHIR-26685 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification BR&R R5 issue asking the work group to resolve ambiguity around product.status, including which codes to use and whether the status represented the product, the record, marketing approval, marketing availability, or another lifecycle concept.
initial_application: No source commit in this checkout directly mentions FHIR-26685. The relevant status work appears in the same medication-definition status history: FHIR-26658 added packaged-product status/statusDate support in April 2020, and later R4B/R5 BR&R status decisions such as FHIR-31780 and FHIR-31790 moved medication-definition status fields toward the draft/active/retired/unknown PublicationStatus pattern.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists MedicinalProductDefinition, PackagedProductDefinition, RegulatedAuthorization, and related medication-definition resources as active current-build resources. MedicinalProductDefinition.status now means the status of the product record/content lifecycle, PackagedProductDefinition.status follows the same pattern, and RegulatedAuthorization.status separately represents authorized/marketing authorization status. FHIR-31790 later tightened product and packaged-product statuses to required code values bound to PublicationStatus and is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build already expresses the resolved separation between product or pack record lifecycle status and marketing authorization status.

related_jiras.note: Added PackagedProductDefinition status/statusDate, part of the R4B/R5 medication-definition status work that resolved the umbrella product.status concern.
